title: Hub-and-Spoke Route Topology with Workspace Lenses
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Problem: Redwood Console navigation has grown organically and users report friction when moving between tenant-level views (billing, org settings) and product surfaces (dashboards, rollouts, cost breakdowns). Current left-nav and ad-hoc top bars create duplicated entry points and inconsistent context when multiple workspaces are active. Goal: Deliver a consolidated route topology that treats the Console as a hub with contextual workspace 'lenses' that surface relevant routes (dashboards, rollouts, cost views, model catalog) without duplicating routes across multiple UI chrome. Scope: information architecture, primary and secondary route mapping, workspace-focused lens UI (compact header dropdown + ephemeral lens bar), prototype flows for: - switching active workspace context (preserve unsaved filters) - navigating to rollout pipelines and canary controls - drilling into token-level cost breakdowns from a host dashboard - path aliasing for deep links and bookmarked views Constraints: must work with existing RBAC and SSO flows, not require backend schema changes for routing, and preserve analytics/tracing hooks. Out-of-scope: rebuilding the authorization model, server-side routing changes beyond alias mapping. Deliverables: IA diagram, 3 interactive Figma prototypes (desktop primary, narrow-screen compact, keyboard-first), annotated acceptance criteria, and a short dev-handoff doc noting edge cases and fallback patterns.
acceptance_criteria: Primary hub page must list top-level tenant surfaces and surface direct links to per-workspace dashboards
Workspace lens selection persists across navigation and is visible in the compact header within 100px of top-left
Deep-linking: a shared URL to a workspace-specific dashboard reproduces the lens and all filters in at most 2 redirects
Performance: new nav chrome must not add more than 30ms to initial route render on average (measured in staging)
Usability: in moderated testing (n=8), average time to open a rollout and toggle canary < 18s
Backward compatibility: existing bookmarked URLs continue to resolve to an equivalent view or a clear migration modal
decisions: Adopt 'hub-and-spoke' topology rather than flattening all routes into a single linear rail to reduce cognitive load
Implement workspace lenses as a transient UI layer (client-side state + URL fragment) instead of creating separate top-level routes for every workspace view
Place cost breakdown quick-access under a consolidated 'Financials' spoke to avoid duplicate 'Cost' items in other surfaces
Use route aliasing on the client to preserve legacy URLs and map them to the new lens-aware routes with deterministic fallback
feedback: PM (Jordan Blake): prefer stronger affordance for cross-workspace comparisons; recommend adding a 2-up compare mode in next iteration
Engineering (Ravi Patel): concerned about preserving KV cache behavior on fast route switches — suggested gating aggressive prefetch behind a flag
Security (Nora Singh): request audit logging hook when a lens is applied to a shared deep-link (added to dev-handoff)
Support (Diego Alvarez): flagged several customer tickets where bookmark UX failed; recommends a migration banner with rollback path
next_steps: Incorporate review feedback and produce v2 prototypes focused on cross-workspace compare
Hand off annotated Figma frames + redlines to ENG for an initial feature flagged implementation (target runtime: console-2025.04)
Schedule 30-minute sync with Platform infra to validate aliasing approach and analytics preservation (owner: Ravi Patel)
Run moderated usability tests (n=8) with current customers who use rollouts and cost dashboards
Prepare short copy for migration banner and user-facing migration help article
